Condition number of a model (collinearity diagnostic)

Source: R/condition_number.R
condition_number.Rd

Computes the condition number of a generalized linear model, following one of four definitions chosen with method. By default (method = "WS") it follows Weissfeld and Sereika (1991): the model is fitted on the original design matrix and the information matrix \(X'\hat{W}X\) at convergence is rescaled so that its diagonal is all ones, which is equivalent to scaling the IRLS-weighted design matrix \(\hat{W}^{1/2}X\) to unit length by column, without centering. This generalizes to any GLM family and link function the classical condition number of linear regression. The other definitions are the one of MacKinnon and Puterman (1989), the one of the original (unweighted) design matrix \(X'X\), and the one of the untransformed information matrix \(X'\hat{W}X\).

Usage

condition_number(model, ...)

# S3 method for class 'glmnet'
condition_number(
  model,
  x,
  y,
  family,
  s,
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  method = c("WS", "MP", "X", "RAW"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'cv.glmnet'
condition_number(
  model,
  x,
  y,
  family,
  s = "lambda.min",
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  method = c("WS", "MP", "X", "RAW"),
  ...
)

Arguments

model

A glm, glmnet or cv.glmnet object.

...

Additional arguments passed to the methods (see x, y, family, s, weights, offset for glmnet/cv.glmnet).

x

Predictor matrix (the same one used to fit the glmnet model), with colnames.

y

Response variable used to fit the glmnet model.

family

GLM family (a family object, e.g. Gamma(link = "inverse")) used to refit a glm on the active set of variables at the given lambda.

s

Lambda value (numeric) for a glmnet object. For cv.glmnet it can also be "lambda.min" or "lambda.1se".

weights

Optional prior weights for the refit.

offset

Optional offset for the refit.

method

One of "WS" (default), "MP", "X" or "RAW". See Details.

Value

An object of class multicollglm_cn with the eigenvalues of the matrix defined by method (eigenvalues), the condition number as the ratio between the largest and the smallest eigenvalue (condition_number), its square root on the classical singular-value scale (condition_index), the variable names (var_names), the method used (method) and its label (nc_label, e.g. "NC_WS"). If the matrix is exactly rank-deficient (perfect collinearity), the condition number is Inf and a warning is issued.

Details

Methods

Let \(X\) be the design matrix (including the intercept column, if any), \(\hat{W}\) the diagonal matrix of IRLS weights at convergence, and let the subscript \(ul\) denote scaling every column to unit Euclidean length. None of the four methods centers the data, so the intercept always takes part in the diagnostic and non-essential collinearity (between the intercept and the explanatory variables) can be detected.

methodMatrix whose eigenvalues are usedReference
"WS" (default)\((X'\hat{W}X)_{ul} = S\,X'\hat{W}X\,S\), with \(S = \mathrm{diag}(X'\hat{W}X)^{-1/2}\)Weissfeld and Sereika (1991)
"MP"\(X_{ul}'\hat{W}X_{ul}\), with \(X\) scaled to unit length before refitting the modelMacKinnon and Puterman (1989)
"X"\(X_{ul}'X_{ul}\): the original design matrix, no weightsBelsley, Kuh and Welsch (1980); \(\kappa_X\) of Lesaffre and Marx (1993)
"RAW"\(X'\hat{W}X\): no transformation at all–

  • "WS" fits the GLM on the raw X and rescales afterwards. Under orthogonality in the GLM metric (\(X'\hat{W}X\) diagonal) it attains its minimum value, 1, for any weights, exactly as the unit-length condition number does in the linear model. This is the recommended definition.

  • "MP" scales X to unit length first, refits the GLM on that matrix (this is done internally) and reads the information matrix off the refit. Because the weights enter after the scaling, the result is 1 under orthogonality only if all the weights are equal.

  • "X" ignores the model's weights, so it measures the collinearity of the explanatory variables themselves, not of the information matrix. It is what a linear-model diagnostic computes on the same predictors, e.g. VisCollin::colldiag(mod, add.intercept = TRUE).

  • "RAW" is the baseline without any transformation. It depends on the units of the explanatory variables and is usually far larger than the others, even when the underlying collinearity is the same.

The condition number is returned on two scales, as in the literature: condition_number, the ratio \(\lambda_{max}/\lambda_{min}\) of the eigenvalues, and condition_index, its square root, which is the classical condition number computed from the singular values of the matrix. Thresholds such as 10 (weak), 30 (moderate to strong) or 100 (Belsley, Kuh and Welsch, 1980) are stated on the square-root scale.

Removed in version 0.4.0

method = "OZ" (Ozkale, 2021) and method = "MS" (Marx and Smith, 1990), as well as the arguments center and scale, no longer exist. All of them centered the data, which removes the intercept from the analysis and so rules out the detection of non-essential collinearity.

References

Belsley, D.A., Kuh, E. and Welsch, R.E. (1980). Regression Diagnostics: Identifying Influential Data and Sources of Collinearity. Wiley.

Lesaffre, E. and Marx, B.D. (1993). Collinearity in generalized linear regression. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 22(7), 1933-1952. doi:10.1080/03610929308831126

MacKinnon, M.J. and Puterman, M.L. (1989). Collinearity in generalized linear models. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 18(9), 3463-3472. doi:10.1080/03610928908830102

Weissfeld, L.A. and Sereika, S.M. (1991). A multicollinearity diagnostic for generalized linear models. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 20(4), 1183-1198. doi:10.1080/03610929108830558

See also

bkw_diagnostics(), rvif_diagnostics(), ml_collinearity().

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 200
x1 <- rnorm(n); x2 <- x1 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.05); x3 <- rnorm(n); x4 <- rnorm(n)
mu <- exp(1 + 0.3 * x1 + 0.3 * x2 - 0.2 * x3 + 0.1 * x4)
y <- rgamma(n, shape = 5, rate = 5 / mu)
mod <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4, family = Gamma(link = "inverse"))

condition_number(mod) # Weissfeld and Sereika (1991), the default
#> Eigenvalues of (X'WX)_ul (decreasing order):
#> [1] 3.2659 0.8814 0.6208 0.2315 0.0003
#> 
#> CN (NC_WS, eigenvalue scale): 10123.1410
#> sqrt(CN) (NC_WS, classical, singular-value scale): 100.6138

# The four definitions side by side (sqrt scale)
sapply(c("WS", "MP", "X", "RAW"),
       function(m) condition_number(mod, method = m)$condition_index)
#>        WS        MP         X       RAW 
#> 100.61382  85.27354  36.97273  86.93647
